scenes.tts: Which phase is each cell in? Freeze this dish of thousands: every cell looks unlabelled, but each carries clues.
scenes.narration: Which phase is each cell in? Freeze this dish of thousands: every cell looks unlabelled, but each carries clues.
scenes.caption: Which phase is each cell in? Freeze this dish of thousands: every cell looks unlabelled, but each carries clues.
scenes.visual: Hook first: a wide dish fills about 80% of the frame height, holding about forty round grey cells that breathe gently. Each cell carries a tiny scrubber dot moving around its own cycle at a different place. The question 'Which phase is each cell in?' appears immediately. On 'freeze', every dot stops at once with a soft white flash, while slow breathing continues.

scenes.tts: In chapter one, one cell's kinase rose and fell once. Its genome was copied once. So DNA doubles once per cycle, then halves at division.
scenes.narration: In chapter 1, one cell's kinase rose and fell once. Its genome was copied once. So DNA doubles once per cycle, then halves at division.
scenes.caption: In chapter 1, one cell's kinase rose and fell once. Its genome was copied once. So DNA doubles once per cycle, then halves at division.
scenes.visual: One frozen cell enlarges into THE WORLD from chapter 1 in the same place: left 60%, the large round cell with its grey nucleus and schematic TEAL DNA bundle; right 40%, the record with the white scrubber and the GREEN 'CDK activity' trace. Show the trace before naming it. The scrubber runs one cycle: green flat, snap, crash. The counter beside the nucleus reads 'copies this cycle: 1'. A TEAL trace labelled 'DNA per cell' is drawn under the green one: flat at '2C' through G1, rising through S as the DNA bundle copies, flat at '4C' through G2 and M, then dropping to '2C' as the cell divides. The right daughter slides off-frame; the left remains. Both traces carry the label 'schematic'.
Title 'A Snapshot of the Cycle' fades in over the dish for 2 s while the frozen cells breathe; the question card fades out under it.

scenes.tts: Start with DNA content. One C is one haploid genome's DNA. A diploid cell holds two C in G one, and four C in G two and mitosis.
scenes.narration: Start with DNA content. One C is one haploid genome's DNA. A diploid cell holds 2C in G1, and 4C in G2 and mitosis.
scenes.caption: Start with DNA content. One C is one haploid genome's DNA. A diploid cell holds 2C in G1, and 4C in G2 and mitosis.
scenes.visual: Show, then tell: zoom into three cells from the dish lined up in a row, labelled G1, S and G2 (phase tags in white, size 28+). Each nucleus holds TEAL DNA: one strand set in G1, a partly doubled set in S, a full doubled set in G2. Under each, a TEAL bar fills to its DNA amount. On 'One C', a small tick on the bar scale labelled '1C = one haploid genome'. On 'two C', the G1 bar locks at a mark '2C'; on 'four C', the G2 bar locks at '4C'. The S bar sits between, its fill creeping upward. A small grey note under the G2 cell: 'still diploid'.

scenes.tts: The cell has not become tetraploid. It still has two homologous sets of chromosomes. By G two, each chromosome has two sister chromatids, doubling DNA without changing ploidy. C measures DNA amount, not chromosome-set number.
scenes.narration: The cell has not become tetraploid. It still has two homologous sets of chromosomes. By G2, each chromosome has two sister chromatids, doubling DNA without changing ploidy. C measures DNA amount, not chromosome-set number.
scenes.caption: The cell has not become tetraploid. It still has two homologous sets of chromosomes. By G2, each chromosome has two sister chromatids, doubling DNA without changing ploidy. C measures DNA amount, not chromosome-set number.
scenes.visual: Keep the G1 and G2 cells and their 2C and 4C bars. Above each bar, show the same two homologous chromosome colours as simple schematic rods; in G2, each rod has a matching sister beside it. Do not draw DNA or protein molecular structures. Transform the 2C bar into 4C while a separate label stays fixed at 'diploid'. Then replace the bars with the compact contrast 'DNA amount: doubled' and 'ploidy: unchanged'.

scenes.tts: Stain fixed cells with propidium iodide, a dye that fluoresces when bound to nucleic acid. Add RNase, because the dye also binds RNA. A flow cytometer reads each cell's fluorescence.
scenes.narration: Stain fixed cells with propidium iodide, a dye that fluoresces when bound to nucleic acid. Add RNase, because the dye also binds RNA. A flow cytometer reads each cell's fluorescence.
scenes.caption: Stain fixed cells with propidium iodide, a dye that fluoresces when bound to nucleic acid. Add RNase, because the dye also binds RNA. A flow cytometer reads each cell's fluorescence.
scenes.visual: The dish cells take on a TEAL glow inside each nucleus, brighter where there is more DNA (label 'propidium iodide'). On 'RNase', faint teal haze in the cytoplasm of each cell fades away, leaving only the nuclear glow. Then a narrow vertical channel (a labelled block 'flow cytometer', no apparatus detail) appears at the right edge; cells stream through it single file. Each cell passing a small white beam flashes, and a matching dot drops onto an empty horizontal axis below labelled 'DNA per cell (glow)'.

scenes.tts: After RNA is removed, fluorescence is a proxy for DNA amount. Under the same staining conditions, a four C cell gives about twice a two C cell's signal. The comparison needs single cells measured consistently.
scenes.narration: After RNA is removed, fluorescence is a proxy for DNA amount. Under the same staining conditions, a 4C cell gives about twice a 2C cell's signal. The comparison needs single cells measured consistently.
scenes.caption: After RNA is removed, fluorescence is a proxy for DNA amount. Under the same staining conditions, a 4C cell gives about twice a 2C cell's signal. The comparison needs single cells measured consistently.
scenes.visual: Keep the cytometer channel. First pass one 2C cell and place its dot over the 2C tick. Then pass one 4C cell with twice the schematic TEAL nuclear signal and place its dot over the 4C tick, twice as far from zero. A small bracket between the ticks reads 'about 2× signal'. Cells continue through one at a time; do not draw internal machinery.

scenes.tts: The dots pile up into a histogram. There is a peak at two C and another at four C. Cells in S spread between them, partway through copying.
scenes.narration: The dots pile up into a histogram. There is a peak at 2C and another at 4C. Cells in S spread between them, partway through copying.
scenes.caption: The dots pile up into a histogram. There is a peak at 2C and another at 4C. Cells in S spread between them, partway through copying.
scenes.visual: The falling dots stack into bars and settle into a computed illustrative histogram filling the right 60% of the frame: peaks centred at 2C and 4C, joined by a broad S-phase bridge. Use area proportions 55% under the 2C peak, 25% between and 20% under the 4C peak; label the corner 'illustrative numbers'. Show the shape first. Then tint the left peak TEAL-light and label it '2C: G0 + G1'; tint the right peak and label it '4C: G2 + M'; tint the bridge and label it 'S'. The dish stays at left and keeps breathing.

scenes.tts: Read the axes before the labels. Horizontal position is fluorescence per cell, used here for DNA amount. Bar height is the number of cells. This plot is a population snapshot, not one cell moving through time.
scenes.narration: Read the axes before the labels. Horizontal position is fluorescence per cell, used here for DNA amount. Bar height is the number of cells. This plot is a population snapshot, not one cell moving through time.
scenes.caption: Read the axes before the labels. Horizontal position is fluorescence per cell, used here for DNA amount. Bar height is the number of cells. This plot is a population snapshot, not one cell moving through time.
scenes.visual: Keep the histogram. Reveal the horizontal label 'DNA per cell (fluorescence)' before the narrator names it, then the vertical label 'number of cells'. A white cursor moves horizontally from 2C to 4C without implying time. Next, dots from several different dish cells drop vertically into their bars at once. A small label 'one snapshot' replaces the cursor; the histogram remains marked 'illustrative numbers'.

scenes.tts: Here is one cell from the four C peak. It has copied all its DNA. Is it still in G two, or already in mitosis?
scenes.narration: Here is one cell from the 4C peak. It has copied all its DNA. Is it still in G2, or already in mitosis?
scenes.caption: Here is one cell from the 4C peak. It has copied all its DNA. Is it still in G2, or already in mitosis?
scenes.visual: A single dot in the 4C peak brightens and lifts out; it grows back into a round cell beside the histogram, its nucleus glowing teal, with its chromosomes hidden behind a soft frosted panel. Question card at top in white: 'G2 or mitosis?'
Predict pause. 'G2 or mitosis?' stays on screen. Near-stillness by design: the lifted cell breathes slowly and the 4C peak shimmers faintly.

scenes.tts: The histogram cannot say. Mitotic cells share the four C peak with G two. Quiescent G zero cells share the two C peak with G one. DNA content narrows the phase; other markers can separate some look-alikes.
scenes.narration: The histogram cannot say. Mitotic cells share the 4C peak with G2. Quiescent G0 cells share the 2C peak with G1. DNA content narrows the phase; other markers can separate some look-alikes.
scenes.caption: The histogram cannot say. Mitotic cells share the 4C peak with G2. Quiescent G0 cells share the 2C peak with G1. DNA content narrows the phase; other markers can separate some look-alikes.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. The frosted panel stays on the lifted cell. Over the 4C peak, translucent labels 'G2' and 'M' occupy the same position, with no visual boundary between them. Over the 2C peak, 'G1' and 'G0' overlap in the same way; a compact label reads 'G0: quiescent'. White rings circle both ambiguous peaks. End with the guiding sentence on screen: 'DNA narrows the phase'.

scenes.tts: Two more stains help. E d U is a thymidine look-alike. During a short pulse, cells copying DNA build it in, and click chemistry adds a glowing tag. It marks cells in S.
scenes.narration: Two more stains help. EdU is a thymidine look-alike. During a short pulse, cells copying DNA build it in, and click chemistry adds a glowing tag. It marks cells in S.
scenes.caption: Two more stains help. EdU is a thymidine look-alike. During a short pulse, cells copying DNA build it in, and click chemistry adds a glowing tag. It marks cells in S.
scenes.visual: Back to the dish at left. A brief wash of small YELLOW dots labelled 'EdU pulse' flows over the dish and is cleared away. Only cells that were copying keep YELLOW specks in their schematic TEAL DNA bundles; a second step labelled 'click tag' makes those specks glow. On the histogram, the broad S-phase bridge lights YELLOW. Keep slow motion in the dish and do not draw EdU's molecular structure.

scenes.tts: EdU also catches cells at the borders. Early S cells can sit near the two C peak, and late S cells near four C. DNA content can blur both into neighbouring phases; EdU reveals ongoing synthesis.
scenes.narration: EdU also catches cells at the borders. Early S cells can sit near the 2C peak, and late S cells near 4C. DNA content can blur both into neighbouring phases; EdU reveals ongoing synthesis.
scenes.caption: EdU also catches cells at the borders. Early S cells can sit near the 2C peak, and late S cells near 4C. DNA content can blur both into neighbouring phases; EdU reveals ongoing synthesis.
scenes.visual: Keep the EdU-positive dish and histogram. First brighten a thin YELLOW inner edge beside the 2C peak and label it 'early S'. Then brighten the inner edge beside 4C and label it 'late S'. The labels transform into one bracket, 'S at the edges', while the central S bridge continues a slow shimmer.

scenes.tts: An antibody detects histone H three phosphorylated on serine ten. This mark spreads across chromosomes as they condense. It helps find mitotic cells, but it is not an exact boundary.
scenes.narration: An antibody detects histone H3 phosphorylated on serine 10. This mark spreads across chromosomes as they condense. It helps find mitotic cells, but it is not an exact boundary.
scenes.caption: An antibody detects histone H3 phosphorylated on serine 10. This mark spreads across chromosomes as they condense. It helps find mitotic cells, but it is not an exact boundary.
scenes.visual: The frosted panel lifts from the cell taken from the 4C peak. Its schematic condensed chromosomes gain a MAGENTA outline labelled 'phospho-H3'; represent the antibody only as a labelled detection tag, never as a molecular structure. Several MAGENTA-positive dots brighten within the 4C peak, but do not split away or leave a clean G2/M boundary. A compact label reads 'mitosis-enriched'.

scenes.tts: The signal begins near centromeres in late G two, before mitosis. It spreads by prophase, remains strong through metaphase, then fades during anaphase. So a positive cell is usually mitotic, but timing keeps the call approximate.
scenes.narration: The signal begins near centromeres in late G2, before mitosis. It spreads by prophase, remains strong through metaphase, then fades during anaphase. So a positive cell is usually mitotic, but timing keeps the call approximate.
scenes.caption: The signal begins near centromeres in late G2, before mitosis. It spreads by prophase, remains strong through metaphase, then fades during anaphase. So a positive cell is usually mitotic, but timing keeps the call approximate.
scenes.visual: A schematic phase strip replaces the histogram: late G2, prophase, metaphase and anaphase. A MAGENTA band starts faintly in late G2, grows across prophase, stays strong through metaphase and fades gradually across anaphase. Keep the strip labelled 'schematic'. Above it, one simple chromosome symbol gains central MAGENTA spots, then a full outline, then loses the outline; do not draw molecular structure.

scenes.tts: G zero is harder: no single stain marks it cleanly. Together, these measures classify most cycling cells. But G zero versus G one and the G two-mitosis boundary remain imperfect.
scenes.narration: G0 is harder: no single stain marks it cleanly. Together, these measures classify most cycling cells. But G0 versus G1 and the G2-mitosis boundary remain imperfect.
scenes.caption: G0 is harder: no single stain marks it cleanly. Together, these measures classify most cycling cells. But G0 versus G1 and the G2-mitosis boundary remain imperfect.
scenes.visual: Return to the dish and histogram. Each frozen cell gains the most honest compact tag allowed by its signals: 2C-only cells 'G0 or G1?', YELLOW cells 'S', 4C phospho-H3-negative cells 'G2 or late M?', and MAGENTA cells 'late G2 or M'. Keep a small label over the 2C peak, 'no clean G0 marker'. The uncertainty marks stay visible; do not assign exact phases.

scenes.tts: So which phase is each cell in? DNA amount narrows the choices; E d U and phospho-H three sharpen the answer. G zero remains unresolved. How long each phase lasts is the text's next question.
scenes.narration: So which phase is each cell in? DNA amount narrows the choices; EdU and phospho-H3 sharpen the answer. G0 remains unresolved. How long each phase lasts is the text's next question.
scenes.caption: So which phase is each cell in? DNA amount narrows the choices; EdU and phospho-H3 sharpen the answer. G0 remains unresolved. How long each phase lasts is the text's next question.
scenes.visual: Return to the one large cell and the record from chapter 1: GREEN CDK activity and the schematic TEAL DNA-per-cell trace run together. As the scrubber passes the cycle, show 2C in G1, YELLOW EdU during S, 4C in G2 and a MAGENTA signal that starts in late G2 and fades during anaphase. The counter reads 'copies this cycle: 1'. Return to the guiding idea in new words on screen: 'Markers sharpen the answer'. On 'how long', a stopwatch with a question mark appears; show no times.

scenes.line: DNA amount narrows the phase; markers sharpen the answer.
